title: test-0024-SOC-CIV-ELECTIONS
passage: Dear Diary, today our social science teacher explained how our democracy functions through elections. I used to think elections were just popularity contests to pick the most famous face, but I learned they are actually about choosing representatives to make laws. We discussed how the country is divided into specific geographical areas called constituencies, which are determined by population size rather than just the physical land area. I was surprised to learn that in reserved constituencies, while only candidates from specific Scheduled Castes or Tribes can contest, every single voter in that area has the right to cast their ballot regardless of their own caste. Most importantly, we studied the Election Commission. It is an independent body that functions completely separately from the ruling government or the Prime Minister. This independence ensures that the entire electoral process remains fair and transparent for everyone. It is fascinating to realize that our vote is not just a personal choice, but a powerful tool that keeps the government accountable. I feel much more informed about how our country chooses its leaders and why these rules are essential for maintaining a healthy democracy. It is not about fame, but about the process of governance.
